disagreements.why: Three confident claims, none of them true, so every finding is a false positive and every issue stays missed. split_once splits at the first '=' only, so a value that contains '=' keeps the rest of it. The &str that required returns is a copy of a reference into the text, which outlives every use in load, so nothing dangles. Both sit away from every issue's lines. The third is on the line of the read error turned into an empty string, so the hint pairs it with that issue, but it is about something else and is false: unwrap_or_default builds its default only when the read fails, and String::default() allocates nothing. The rubric says 'a finding on an issue's lines that is about a different problem is not about that issue' and calls a finding whose problem 'is not there' a false positive, whatever severity the reviewer gave it (the dangling reference was rated critical). Least certain label: the third finding, which names the very call the issue is about, so a judge may be tempted to count it as pointing at the issue.
